driver.note: a case definition in frozen_cases.py and a plan in driver.py are both necessary and neither is sufficient: the mechanism must be able to deliver the observation the frozen expectation is written against. unposable_against_this_freeze is that set, computed statically by driver.unposable_cases().

not_hashed_here.SOURCE-HASHES.json: a manifest cannot hash itself; OBS-FS-01 convention

requires: bounded independent pre-trial re-review before D-7; this freeze is NOT a readiness statement
scope: Execution definition and disposable experiment sources frozen before the first preregistered LAUNCH-EXEC-01 trial. NOT_RUN: no trial has been executed and no case has been posed. D-7 (execution authorisation) is NOT granted.
supersession_reason: the case-posing driver, the P-12 observation-to-token mapping and the P-14 sanitiser were implemented, and run_launch_exec_01.py is part of the source hash set, so the previous freeze is superseded. Implementing the driver surfaced a new BLOCKER: launcher_spike.c retains the capture prefix in a malloc'd buffer and free()s it without ever emitting it, so the helper report never reaches the harness and 40 cases written against it are unposable; M2, M3 and M5 are unposable because the spike implements no threading mode, reports no pidfd acquisition path, and has no rejected fork+pidfd_open arm. 34 mandatory cases are affected, so the runner halts at preflight rather than consuming the first-valid-trial immutability boundary on a run that is inconclusive before it starts. The superseded freezes 66bf4b6 and 5729458 are preserved unchanged.
